name: Semiya Upma
cuisine: South Indian (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala breakfast; also common in Maharashtra homes)

ingredients.name: Wheat vermicelli, roasted or plain (semiya, seviyan)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ½ cup of broken pieces (varies by brand; weigh it if you can)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion, thinly sliced or chopped (about ¼ cup)

equipment: Kadai or wide non-stick pan with a lid (about 20 cm)
Small saucepan or electric kettle, to heat the water
Wooden spoon or spatula (non-stick safe) and a fork for fluffing
Knife and chopping board, measuring spoons, a kitchen scale (or use the spoon measures given)
Grater or small mortar for the ginger

steps.title: Break the semiya
steps.text: Measure 50 g wheat vermicelli. If the strands are long, break them into 2–3 cm pieces with your hands.
steps.visualCue: Short, even pieces, about ½ cup
steps.cameraCheck: The measured semiya on a plate
steps.videoShot: Hands snapping long semiya strands into short pieces.

steps.title: Dry-roast the semiya
steps.text: Put the semiya in a dry kadai on low heat and stir constantly. Hebbar's Kitchen and Swasthi both roast it even when it is sold "roasted".
steps.tip: Keep the flame low and keep stirring; it burns in seconds. Roasting is what keeps the strands from going sticky.
steps.visualCue: Strands turn a shade darker golden and smell nutty
steps.cameraCheck: The roasted semiya on a plate next to the unroasted one
steps.videoShot: Semiya stirred in the dry kadai as it darkens.

steps.title: Cool the semiya
steps.text: Tip the roasted semiya onto a plate and wipe the kadai.
steps.videoShot: Roasted semiya tipped onto a plate.

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Slice ½ small onion (40 g), dice 25 g carrot finely, slit 1 green chilli, and grate ½-inch ginger.
steps.tip: Dice the carrot very small; it must cook in about 2 min.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces so they cook in the short time
steps.cameraCheck: The four prepared items in small bowls
steps.videoShot: Knife dicing a carrot into tiny cubes.

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.text: Heat 200 ml water until it is boiling hot, and keep it nearby.
steps.cameraCheck: The hot water in a pot or kettle
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from the hot water.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat 1½ tsp (7 g) oil in the kadai on medium.
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled in a hot kadai.

steps.title: Pop the mustard seeds
steps.text: Add ½ tsp (1 g) mustard seeds.
steps.tip: Keep a lid nearby to stop seeds jumping out.
steps.visualCue: Seeds crackle and jump; stop at the first fast popping
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds popping in the oil.

steps.title: Fry the dal and cashews
steps.text: Add ½ tsp (2 g) urad dal and 4 broken cashews (6 g).
steps.visualCue: Dal and cashew turn light golden, not brown
steps.cameraCheck: The golden dal and cashews in the oil
steps.videoShot: Cashews turning gold in the kadai.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Add 8–10 curry leaves, the slit chilli and the grated ginger.
steps.tip: Curry leaves spit; add them with your arm held back.
steps.visualCue: Leaves crackle and the kitchen smells sharp and fresh
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with leaves and chilli
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves sizzling in the oil.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: Onion turns soft and see-through, not brown (Swasthi and Hebbar's Kitchen both say not to brown it)
steps.cameraCheck: The translucent onion in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Onion turning glossy and soft in the pan.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add 25 g diced carrot, 20 g green peas and a pinch of turmeric, and stir.
steps.visualCue: Peas bright green, carrot slightly softer and shiny
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed vegetables in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Carrot and peas tossed in the pan.

steps.title: Add the hot water and salt
steps.text: Pour in the 200 ml hot water and add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt. Bring it to a rolling boil.
steps.tip: Taste the water: it should taste slightly salty, like light soup.
steps.visualCue: Big bubbles over the whole surface
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling water in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Water bubbling hard in the kadai.

steps.title: Add the semiya
steps.text: Lower the heat to low. Sprinkle the roasted semiya into the boiling water in a thin stream, stirring as you add it.
steps.tip: Adding the semiya only once the water is boiling is what stops clumping (a tip from several of the recipe sites).
steps.visualCue: All strands wet and sinking into the water, no dry clumps
steps.cameraCheck: The semiya stirred into the water
steps.videoShot: Semiya poured in a thin stream while a spoon stirs.

steps.title: Cover and cook
steps.text: Cover the kadai and cook on low.
steps.tip: If it looks dry but the strands are still hard, sprinkle 1–2 tbsp hot water, cover, and cook 1 min more.
steps.visualCue: Most of the water has been absorbed and the strands are soft when pressed with a spoon
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful of semiya lifted to show soft strands
steps.videoShot: Lid lifted, steam rising from the cooked semiya.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the lid on.
steps.visualCue: Strands look separate, not wet or pasty
steps.videoShot: Lid closed on the kadai, steam leaking out.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Squeeze in 1 tsp (5 ml) lemon juice, add 1 tsp chopped coriander and fluff gently with a fork.
steps.visualCue: Separate, glossy strands with flecks of green
steps.cameraCheck: The finished upma in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Fork lifting the upma to show loose strands.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate while hot with coconut chutney or sambar.
steps.visualCue: A loose, fluffy mound with cashews and peas showing
steps.videoShot: Plate of semiya upma with a spoon of chutney.

reasons: no frying, only 7 g oil, no ghee, no cholesterol, low saturated fat (about 1.4 g) and vegetables and cashew in a short cook. Points off because it is mostly refined-wheat noodle with only about 9.5 g protein and 4.5 g fibre, and a moderate 605 mg sodium. Restaurant and tiffin-centre versions usually use more oil or ghee and often fewer vegetables, so the plate is heavier and lower in fibre (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published South Indian breakfast that nearly every major Indian recipe site and blog carries (Hebbar's Kitchen, Indian Healthy Recipes, Veg Recipes of India, Archana's Kitchen, Tarla Dalal, Sharmi's Passions, Subbus Kitchen), described as quick, 15–25 min and kid-friendly. Points off because the recipe pages could not be opened here, so vote counts and star averages could not be read; the dish also has a reputation for turning sticky or bland if the water ratio is wrong, and it is a lighter, less loved cousin of rava upma. The number is an estimate from how widely and consistently it is recommended. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Best eaten fresh, because the strands keep absorbing moisture. Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 1 day (cool within 1 hour). Freezing is not recommended (the strands turn mushy). Reheat in a pan on low with 1–2 tbsp water, covered, 2–3 min; or microwave covered with a splash of water for 1 min.
leftoverRemix: Semiya upma cutlet. Mash the cold leftover upma with 1 boiled mashed potato (or 2 tbsp roasted besan if avoiding potato), a pinch of chaat masala and chopped coriander; shape into small patties and shallow-roast on a tawa with ½ tsp oil until crisp on both sides.
burnOff: about 4.8 km of running (335 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.7 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 20 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: wheat vermicelli is a grain product, and the recipe also uses onion, mustard and table salt, which the common rule set avoids (the common rule set uses sabudana, kuttu or singhare instead).

ekadashi.reason: vermicelli is made from wheat (or rice), and grains are avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set.

jain.reason: drop the onion, fresh ginger and carrot and use capsicum or beans, dry ginger powder (sonth) and hing, as in the Jain variant.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; it is light, quick and filling. Salt is moderate (about 605 mg sodium) but protein is only about 9.5 g, so add curd, sprouts or a dal side at sehri.

jain.reason: the main recipe uses onion, fresh ginger and carrot (roots); drop all three (use capsicum or French beans, dry ginger powder and hing) as in the Jain variant.

vegan.reason: made with oil, no ghee, curd, milk or egg. Check the vermicelli label: a few brands (egg semiya, mostly in Kerala) contain egg.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: garlic is not used; leave out the 40 g onion (use capsicum or beans) and do not add hing if you follow a strict sattvik rule.

glutenFree.reason: wheat vermicelli contains gluten. Use the Gluten-free variant (rice vermicelli), and skip hing or use a gluten-free one, because most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: no milk, ghee, curd or paneer in the main recipe (some recipes finish with a spoon of ghee; leave it out).
